title: FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts' only. Does not supplant organization-wide SIEM playbooks for unrelated threat classes or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `soc_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `security_infra_fortigate_resource_utilization_alerts` (UC-10.11.13), SOC dashboard panel "Security Infra — FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:soc_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=metrics` sourcetype='fortinet:fortigate_snmp' where `host` satisfies `cpu` > 85 for UC-10.11.13 ('FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `metrics` / `fortinet:fortigate_snmp` events where `host` stays below `cpu` > 85, or exclude the test entity via `soc_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-10.11.13.

dataSources: `sourcetype=fortinet:fortigate_snmp` Collected via Splunk Add-on for Fortinet FortiGate (Splunkbase 2846) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.

description: Resource pressure can cause dropped logs, missed inspection, and HA instability. Searches `index=metrics` with sourcetype `fortinet:fortigate_snmp` for UC-10.11.13, aggregating `avg` by `host` over `the scheduled window`. Alerts when grouped results cross `cpu` > 85 in the saved search. Gives Security Infra operators a repeatable signal for 'FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts' without manual log review.
value: Early 'FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts' detection reduces missed threat campaigns, control regressions, and SOC SLA breaches by giving Security Infra operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Ingest SNMP or streaming metrics for CPU, memory, and session table. Threshold alert before performance degrades inspection.
visualization: Single value (CPU/mem), Line chart (utilization), Table (top busy devices).
cimSpl: | tstats summariesonly=t avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value from datamodel=Performance.Network by Performance.host | sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM `Performance.Network` dataset after normalizing this feed to the model; otherwise the `cimSpl` tstats search may return no rows.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `metrics`** — Planned work for 'FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts' shifts `avg` over `span=1h` while `host` remains in-scope for UC-10.11.13. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `avg` on `fortinet:fortigate_snmp`** — Scheduled automation elevates `src` without crossing `cpu` > 85. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `host`** — Health checks in `metrics` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `fortinet:fortigate_snmp`** — First 48h baseline for `host` is unstable; window via `soc_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `soc_exception_register.csv` keyed on `host`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: `Splunk_TA_fortinet`.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=fortinet:fortigate_snmp`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest SNMP or streaming metrics for CPU, memory, and session table. Threshold alert before performance degrades inspection.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=metrics OR index=network sourcetype="fortinet:fortigate_snmp"
| stats avg(cpu_pct) as cpu, avg(mem_used_pct) as mem by host
| where cpu>85 OR mem>90
```

Understanding this SPL

**FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts** — Resource pressure can cause dropped logs, missed inspection, and HA instability.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=fortinet:fortigate_snmp`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Splunk_TA_fortinet`. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: metrics, network; **sourcetype**: fortinet:fortigate_snmp. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Detection type** for this use case: Anomaly — interpret thresholds and fields in that context.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=metrics, index=network, sourcetype="fortinet:fortigate_snmp". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by host** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Filters the current rows with `where cpu>85 OR mem>90` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Optional CIM / accelerated variant (same use case, normalized fields via Common Information Model):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value from datamodel=Performance.Network by Performance.host | sort - agg_value
```

Understanding this CIM / accelerated SPL

**FortiGate Resource Utilization Alerts** — Resource pressure can cause dropped logs, missed inspection, and HA instability.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=fortinet:fortigate_snmp`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Splunk_TA_fortinet`. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

This **CIM or accelerated** block uses normalized field names and/or `tstats` over data models. Enable **acceleration** on the referenced models (and correct CIM knowledge objects) or the search may return nothing.

**Detection type** for this use case: Anomaly — interpret thresholds and fields in that context.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Performance.Network` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Run the search over a window that includes both normal production traffic and, if you have one, a documented test (vendor sandbox, lab rule hit, or exercise). Compare a few sample events to the vendor’s own console or reports and tune indexes, fields, and thresholds so alerts are actionable before paging.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Single value (CPU/mem), Line chart (utilization), Table (top busy devices).
